ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a transition-state structure; on the left is a benzene ring skeleton, and the benzene ring is connected to a CH2 substituent; near the benzene ring there is also a nitro-like fragment, containing N, one N=O, and one N–O; at the upper right there is an OMe fragment. The figure also has curved arrows and charge labels, but the question requires ignoring arrows and not counting bonds involving hydrogen. Then reason and count: Count each non-hydrogen bond in the figure item by item; the benzene ring itself has 6 intra-ring bonds; the CH2 substituent connected to the benzene ring adds 1 C–C bond; the nitro fragment counts as 3 bonds, namely the ring-to-N bond, the N=O bond, and the N–O bond; the OMe fragment counts as 1 O–C bond. The total is 6 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 11.

method.method_draft: Inspect the image and split it into components. The benzene ring contributes 6 bonds. The CH2 substituent attached to the ring adds 1 more bond. The nitro group contributes 3 bonds total: one bond from the ring to N, one N=O bond, and one N–O bond. The OMe fragment contributes 1 O–C bond. Ignore all arrows and any bond to H. Sum: 6 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 11.
